kept.name: Average Hengshun export bottle volume
kept.rationale: US-bound Chinese vinegar is predominantly sold in 500 ml glass bottles with some 300/250 ml; a 0.5 L central value with a 0.35–0.6 L range reflects the mix of retail bottle sizes. The 2020 glass-bottle purchase data (p47/p50) imply an all-product average near 1.1 L/bottle including large formats, so
kept.applies_when: Export packaging is dominated by retail glass bottles in the 250–600 ml range, excluding bulk drums.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that a large share of US-bound volume is bulk/industrial or in much larger retail formats.

kept.name: Hengshun export FOB price per liter (RMB)
kept.rationale: China's average HS 22090000 export unit price is ~1.15 USD/L (p21), i.e. ~8 RMB/L at ~7 RMB/USD; Hengshun is a premium branded Zhenjiang vinegar, so its FOB price should sit above the national average, around 12 RMB/L with a range of 8–18.
kept.applies_when: Hengshun's export price is a premium multiple of the national average unit value.
kept.falsified_by: Disclosed export revenue and volume implying a per-liter price far outside 8–18 RMB.

kept.name: Hengshun share of China HS 22090000 vinegar export volume, 2024
kept.rationale: Hengshun is the largest branded Zhenjiang-vinegar producer but China's vinegar exports are fragmented across many producers and unbranded bulk; a 3% volume share (1–6% range) is a reasonable order-of-magnitude for a leading branded exporter.
kept.applies_when: Hengshun's export volume is a small single-digit share of total Chinese vinegar exports.
kept.falsified_by: Customs or company data showing Hengshun's export volume share outside 1–6%.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
